mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% and remains above for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 500k units for three consecutive months signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 500k for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong labor market growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.4 percentage points over three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.4pp over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of rising inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 1% year-over-year signals a deflationary monetary regime, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of strong credit expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% month-over-month for three consecutive months) combined with rising retail sales (RSAFS growth > 0.5% month-over-month for two months) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.4% MoM for 3 months AND RSAFS > 0.5% MoM for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% for six consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates and ultimately reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% for six consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS rising trend
regime_hint: tight labor market with rising rates
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of falling inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.4% for five consecutive months signals a robust expansion in economic output, which supports higher corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of rising interest rates.
